entries.justification:
D-11 — Phase 156 HWLC-11 advisory firewall (justified in the ledger, NOT fixed). This route renders hardware-lifecycle/vendor risk badges using raw hsl() Tailwind arbitrary-value literals (bg-[hsl(24_95%_53%)] and/or bg-[hsl(142_71%_45%)]) that deliberately bypass the app's semantic score-color design tokens. Per Phase 156 D-07, these literals implement a mechanical firewall between the advisory-only hardware lifecycle / vendor PQC trend section and the app's scored-finding visual language, so an advisory badge can never be visually confused with a real CBOM/QRAMM scored finding (see 156-UI-SPEC.md §Color). That firewall is enforced by two guard tests that pin these exact literals in a FORBIDDEN_PALETTE array and fail if either is retuned toward the app's contrast-compliant palette: src/dashboard/src/components/__tests__/lifecycle-advisory-guard.test.ts (hsl(24 95% 53%) at line 16, hsl(142 71% 45%) at line 18) and src/dashboard/src/components/__tests__/vendor-trend-advisory-guard.test.ts (hsl(24 95% 53%) at line 18, hsl(142 71% 45%) at line 20). Tokenizing or adjusting either literal to satisfy color-contrast would deliberately break both currently-passing guard tests. Per D-11 this violation is accepted here and tracked in this ledger, not fixed; the raw hsl() literals are left unchanged — confirmed by an empty git diff on both component files.

Count-increase addendum (Phase 216, D-05/D-07, REVEALED not created): this route's color-contrast count rose from the prior baseline's 3 to 8 nodes on this regeneration. This is the SAME D-11 Phase-156 firewalled raw-hsl() badge debt described above, now rendering more badge instances because 216-02 enriched the fixture with more hardware vendor/lifecycle records than the pre-216 fixture carried — more rows means more badges using the same two firewalled literals, not a new violation shape. Per 216-CONTEXT.md D-04/D-09, this phase BASELINES this finding rather than fixing it: a phase whose job is instrument repair (fixing the harness's fixture and theme coverage) must not also change product pixels, or a red gate becomes unattributable to either change on its own. This entry is explicitly OUT of FIX-01..FIX-04's scope: the Phase-156 firewall (lifecycle-advisory-guard.test.ts, vendor-trend-advisory-guard.test.ts) deliberately keeps these two literals off the app's semantic token system, so FIX-01's token-pair swap does not apply to them, and FIX-04's named design calls (`--destructive`/`--quantum-safe`/`--badge-modbus`) do not include them either. FIX-05's "zero badge pair anywhere" target does not retire this entry unless a future phase revisits the Phase-156 firewall design itself; that revisit is out of scope here.
